scope: Local candidate ConPTY terminal; no production backend switch, login or paid API request.

conditions.fixture: New temporary profile and tools/work/out directories for each mode.
conditions.executable: System cmd.exe /d /q, followed by native test helpers staged in fixture/tools.
conditions.boundary: Suspended shell token verified before resume; exact package and zero capabilities; mode independently verified with AccessCheck; shell assigned to kill-on-close Job.
conditions.transport: Host owns synchronous pipes and ConPTY; the restricted shell receives console handles, not inherited host stdio. No named-pipe namespace grants were added.

results.ctrlCObservation: The host wrote byte 0x03 to ConPTY input; the foreground native helper received os.Interrupt and printed its completion marker.
results.limitations: This verifies cmd and two fixture helpers. It does not verify PowerShell, Claude Code interactive TUI, arbitrary shells, task termination of every external application or production workbench integration.

results.failureStage: cmd invoking the staged native token helper
results.observedDiagnostic: Access denied in the cmd console; no token-helper marker was produced.
results.failureScope: The native helper was not observed running. This is not evidence of an incorrect child token, and the exact failed Win32 operation was not instrumented.
results.limitations: The LPAC cmd built-in echo path works, but the development terminal requiring external child processes did not pass. No capability or host-path ACL was broadened to force compatibility.

notes: Typed command echo cannot satisfy the input/output markers: marker values are expanded from synthetic fixture environment variables by cmd.
The output reader stays active during Job closure and ClosePseudoConsole, and both runs drained successfully.
The separate terminal-rpc protocol and workbench transport test have their own evidence; this report does not assert their results.
The terminal result does not change the recorded Edge, Desktop or VS Code GUI compatibility failures.
